title: Heating 1.0 kg of water with a 2.0 kW kettle
caption: With Q = mcΔT = 1 × 4180 × 80 = 334 kJ and a power of 2 kW, the water reaches 100 °C after t = Q/P = 167.2 s (about 2.8 min). The line is straight because c is taken as constant and all the power goes into the water, so 0.48 K rise every second: the stated time is a minimum.
alt: Graph of water temperature against time: a straight line from 20 °C at 0 s to 100 °C at 167.2 s.
description: The horizontal axis is time in seconds, the vertical axis is the water temperature in °C.
The temperature rises at P/(mc) = 2000 ÷ (1 × 4180) = 0.48 K s⁻¹, starting at 20 °C.
The line reaches 100 °C at t = 167.2 s, the lesson's answer of about 167 s.

checks.name: the gradient is P/(mc) = 0.48 K per second
